name: Passkey Authentication to Home
summary: The email-resolved user completes a valid user-verified passkey assertion and receives a normal authenticated application session.

preconditions.expression: session-capability == anonymous and a normalized email is retained in authentication flow state and a registered passkey is available for that account

serverInteraction.intent: Resolve the expected account by email, issue a user-bound passkey challenge requiring user verification, validate that the assertion credential belongs to that exact user, advance the signature counter, and establish the platform-appropriate application session.

sourceReferences.note: Email-bound begin/complete endpoints use one proof service, then establish either a browser session or mobile token session after successful proof.
Email resolves the expected durable UserId before challenge issuance and delegates to the user-bound passkey manager with user verification required.
The shared proof validates challenge ownership, credential ownership, WebAuthn assertion and signature counter.
Angular Web consumes the retained login-seed email, uses the generated email-bound begin/complete operations, performs navigator.credentials.get, and follows the authenticated redirect.

React Native begins the email-bound challenge, invokes the native passkey ceremony, maps the assertion to the generated wire contract, completes through the email-bound token operation, persists AuthResponse, restores the token lifecycle, and routes to the authenticated landing destination.
React Native declares native passkey support and the iOS webcredentials association required by the ceremony; domain association files remain deployment infrastructure.
Generated contracts expose typed email-bound passkey begin, browser complete, and mobile token complete operations.
Email-first primary Passkey and Password-then-Passkey MFA intentionally share the same user-bound passkey proof primitive. Direct discoverable Passkey-first sign-in is deferred.

Passkey Authentication to Home is implementation-complete by source inspection across server, Angular Web, Android and iOS. Runtime browser/device execution has not yet been performed, so tests remain not-started.
